candidates.attacker_control: The parsed byte[] in the validator path is the decoded `Library.content.data` Attachment payload chosen by whoever supplies the Library resource (FHIR JSON/XML attachment with contentType `application/elm+xml`). The Library is loaded by the worker context from an untrusted IG/package (`-ig`) or, in a HAPI/JPA-backed deployment, from conformance resources stored in the server; the validating Measure (with `Measure.library` pointing at it) is likewise attacker-supplied. In PackageVisitor.processFeed the same utility parses an XML document fetched over HTTP from a feed URL listed in the ig-registry feed file, i.e., network-controlled content.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The repository shows it knows this class of bug: elementmodel XmlParser (r5, r4b, r4, dstu3, dstu2016may), ValidatorUtils.parseXml, and the older translations parsers set disallow-doctype-decl/external-general-entities=false, and XhtmlParser/InstanceValidator reject DOCTYPE in narratives; XMLUtil was simply left unprotected. Counterarguments considered: (a) `context.fetchResource(Library.class, ...)` must resolve, so the trigger needs a Library that the context has already loaded (IG package or server-stored conformance resource) - this is realistic for IG validation and JPA-backed validation, but not for validating a bare Measure with an unresolvable library reference; (b) the parsed Document is used for structural checks (isValidElm/hasCqlTarget), and parse exceptions are captured as messages, so a direct file-content echo back to the attacker was not identified - the reliable impacts are SSRF, blind/OOB exfiltration and DoS; (c) the other XMLUtil overloads are used on local/registry data, which lowers their individual risk but does not remove the shared root cause. No runtime testing was performed.
candidates.impact: External entity resolution during validation: server-side request forgery/DNS to URLs or `file:` system identifiers chosen by the attacker (external general entities and external DTDs), blind local file disclosure via an external parameter-entity DTD that forwards file content to an attacker-controlled endpoint, and denial of service via entity expansion / recursive entity definitions. The parser executes inside the validator/host process, so it can reach files and network resources available to that process (e.g., conformance data, keystores, metadata endpoints).
candidates.prerequisites: The application must validate attacker-influenced FHIR content with the core validator (CLI, NativeHostServices, or a HAPI server) and the worker context must resolve a `Library` reference whose resource carries an `application/elm+xml` attachment (or, for the PackageVisitor path, process an attacker/registry-controlled XML feed). No special configuration or elevated privilege is required; the XXE executes with the JVM's network/OS-level access.
candidates.root_cause: XMLUtil.parseToDom(String), parseToDom(byte[]), parseToDom(byte[], boolean), parseFileToDom(String) and parseFileToDom(String, boolean) build a javax.xml.parsers.DocumentBuilderFactory with only setNamespaceAware(...) and parse the document with default JAXP settings, so DOCTYPE declarations, external general/parameter entities and external DTD loading remain enabled. Every comparable parser in the repository (r5/r4b/r4/r4b/dstu3/dstu2016may elementmodel XmlParser, validation ValidatorUtils.parseXml) explicitly disables these, so this is an incomplete hardening of the shared XML utility.
candidates.title: XXE in XMLUtil.parseToDom reachable from FHIR Measure/Library validation (application/elm+xml attachment)
candidates.trace: 1) InstanceValidator.validateResource dispatches type "Measure" to new MeasureValidator(...).validateMeasure (InstanceValidator.java:5029-5030). 2) MeasureValidator.validateMeasure iterates Measure.library and calls context.fetchResource(Library.class, ref) (MeasureValidator.java:59-63); Library resources are indexed in the worker context by BaseWorkerContext.seeResource `libraries.see((Library) m, packageInfo)` (BaseWorkerContext.java:479-480) when packages are loaded. 3) For each resolved Library, mctxt.seeLibrary(l) runs (MeasureValidator.java:65). 4) MeasureContext.seeLibrary takes every Attachment with contentType "application/elm+xml" and calls XMLUtil.parseToDom(att.getData(), true) (MeasureContext.java:31-34). 5) XMLUtil.parseToDom(byte[], boolean) creates an unhardened DocumentBuilderFactory and calls builder.parse(...) (XMLUtil.java:450-455), so a DOCTYPE with an external entity in the attachment body is resolved by the default JAXP/Xerces parser.
candidates.unverified: Not verified by execution: the precise JDK/Xerces default behavior in the target runtime (standard JAXP defaults allow DOCTYPE/external entities), whether every deployment's IWorkerContext resolves attacker-created Libraries (HAPI/JPA on-demand loading was not inspectable from this snapshot), and whether an equivalent issue was subsequently fixed upstream. Content of the file(s) disclosed, if any, was not demonstrated.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

coverage_summary: Scope: the full assigned snapshot (7,227 model-visible files, no excluded/symlinked/sensitive files by the source-scope report). Reviewed by targeted reading/search: org.hl7.fhir.utilities (xml/XmlUtil, XhtmlParser, npm package cache/package loading, SimpleHTTPClient/SSLCertTruster, IniFile, zip utilities), the validation module (InstanceValidator, BaseValidator, Measure/MeasureReport/Questionnaire/StructureMap validators, ValidatorUtils, ValidationEngine, IgLoader, Scanner, NativeHostServices, CLI services/renderers), the convertors (version convertors, CDA/CCDA utilities, package analytics, XVersionLoader), and the XML/JSON parsers of dstu2/dstu3/r4/r4b/r5. Generated model classes (tens of thousands of lines of pure getters/setters), RdfParser/JsonParser generated code, and most i18n/test data were only sampled. No execution, tests, scanners or external lookups were performed.
limitations: Read-only, non-executing review: parser behavior (JDK/Xerces default external-entity resolution; xpp3 DTD defaults for the dstu2 gap) is argued from source and documented library semantics, not observed at runtime.

Reachability of MeasureContext.seeLibrary depends on the hosting application's IWorkerContext implementation (HAPI/JPA on-demand conformance-resource loading was outside this snapshot), so the deployment-specific trigger could not be confirmed here.
External dependencies (xpp3/kxml XmlPullParser, Saxon, commons-compress) are not included in the snapshot, so their exact DTD/entity handling could not be inspected.

The repository is very large (7,227 files, multi-megabyte generated parsers/models); review was breadth-first and prioritized security-relevant sinks, so other low-prevalence issues in uninspected generated code cannot be excluded.
No candidate is claimed as a runtime-confirmed vulnerability; the submitted item is an evidence-based lead.

rejected_leads.lead: org.hl7.fhir.dstu2.formats.XmlParserBase.loadXml (lines 206-216) is the only one of the six FHIR version XML parsers that does not call factory.setFeature(XmlPullParser.FEATURE_PROCESS_DOCDECL, false) (compare dstu2016may:210, dstu3:210, r4:234, r4b:220, r5:227).
rejected_leads.reason: Real hardening asymmetry, but exploitability could not be established from this snapshot: it depends on the external xpp3/kXML XmlPullParser's DTD/entity defaults, and the core validator never routes untrusted input through the dstu2 format parser (Manager.makeParser always uses the hardened r5 elementmodel XmlParser). Kept as unconfirmed XXE/entity-expansion lead only.

rejected_leads.lead: SSLCertTruster.trustAllHosts() installs a trust-all X509TrustManager as the JVM default via HttpsURLConnection.setDefaultSSLSocketFactory (SSLCertTruster.java:31-53) and is invoked unconditionally by SimpleHTTPClient.trustAllhosts() from FilesystemPackageCacheManager.loadFromBuildServer() (lines 685-688).
rejected_leads.reason: Definite CWE-295-style weakness with JVM-global side effects, but the call site is a documented, deliberately accepted workaround for build.fhir.org and the only demonstrated impact requires a network man-in-the-middle; not selected as the strongest source-evidenced candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: SimpleHTTPClient.get re-applies credentials on every redirect hop (setHeaders called after each Location is followed, lines 145-179), so Basic auth for a terminology/package server can be sent to a redirect target.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible credential-disclosure bug, but it requires a malicious/compromised redirecting server and configured credentials; weaker and more speculative than the XXE candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Unprotected JAXP/DOM parsers in org.hl7.fhir.convertors.misc.CDAUtilities (lines 53-60), org.hl7.fhir.utilities.xls.XLSXmlParser (169-172), XLSXmlNormaliser (217-221) and TranslatorXml (70-74).
rejected_leads.reason: Same class of sink as the candidate but with no in-repo call path from untrusted service input: CDAUtilities is only reached by the standalone CCDA/Argonaut conversion utilities, and the XLS parsers are used by the out-of-repo IG publisher. Not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: Package/cache extraction path handling (NpmPackage.readStream, FilesystemPackageCacheManager.addPackageToCache, CacheLock, Utilities.unzip, Scanner.unzip).
rejected_leads.reason: Checked and found protected: tar/zip entries containing ".." are rejected and file names pass through Utilities.cleanFileName; no reachable zip-slip/arbitrary write was established. Package-id strings are not validated before cache path construction, but no attacker-controlled source for a traversing id was traced in this snapshot.

summary: Reviewed the org.hl7.fhir.core snapshot (7,227 files; modules utilities, dstu2/dstu3/r4/r4b/r5, convertors, validation, validation.cli, generator). The strongest source-evidenced issue is an XML External Entity (XXE) sink in `org.hl7.fhir.utilities.xml.XMLUtil.parseToDom(...)`: all five overloads create a JAXP `DocumentBuilderFactory` without the XXE protections that every other XML entry point in this repository applies (no `disallow-doctype-decl`, no `external-general-entities=false`, no `expandEntityReferences=false`). This utility is called on attacker-influenced bytes during validation: `InstanceValidator` dispatches `Measure` resources to `MeasureValidator.validateMeasure`, which resolves `Measure.library` references and hands each resolved `Library` to `MeasureContext.seeLibrary`, which parses every `Library.content` attachment whose contentType is `application/elm+xml` with `XMLUtil.parseToDom(att.getData(), true)`. A Library is attacker-supplied in the normal untrusted-content workflows (malicious IG package loaded with `-ig`, or a Library created on a HAPI/JPA-backed server whose validation support chain populates the worker context). Impact is classic XXE: outbound requests/DNS to attacker- or internal-chosen endpoints (SSRF), external-DTD-based file disclosure (blind), and entity-expansion DoS, in the security context of the validator process. I selected this single candidate; the other plausible issues found are listed as rejected/unconfirmed leads.
